project.name: Athena
project.description: Athena is an AI marketing pipeline for UrbanSpace self-storage: a FastAPI + LangGraph backend ingests Meta posts and comments, Google Business reviews, Google Ads keyword volumes and Zoho CRM chat transcripts, then runs AI research and content generation over them (Claude for text, Gemini for images, Canva for the editing handoff). A React + TypeScript dashboard serves the results as weekly KPIs, research tabs and AI-generated post drafts.

nodes.name: .dockerignore
nodes.summary: Excludes local virtualenvs, tests, docs, the deploy directory, node_modules and prebuilt frontend output from the Docker build context so the root-context image build stays small and reproducible.

nodes.name: Dockerfile
nodes.summary: Two-stage whole-app image: a node:22-alpine stage builds the React dashboard, then a python:3.12-slim stage installs the backend with uv and copies the built dashboard in, so the single `api` container serves both the REST API and the dashboard at "/".
nodes.languageNotes: Multi-stage build with `COPY --from=dashboard`; uv dependency layers are split (`--no-install-project` first) so source edits do not invalidate the dependency cache.

nodes.name: dashboard
nodes.summary: First build stage on node:22-alpine that runs `npm ci` and `npm run build` over frontend/ to produce the static dashboard bundle in /fe/dist.

nodes.name: python
nodes.summary: Final runtime stage on python:3.12-slim that uv-syncs the backend from pyproject/uv.lock, copies src, migrations and alembic.ini, and pulls the built dashboard from the node stage.

nodes.name: docker-compose.yml
nodes.summary: Local development stack that builds the image from source and runs Postgres, the API, the worker and a hot-reloading dev console, all published on 127.0.0.1 only.
nodes.languageNotes: Deliberately distinct from deploy/docker-compose.yml: this one builds locally and publishes ports, the production file consumes a prebuilt image on an external network.

nodes.name: db
nodes.summary: Postgres 16 alpine service backing local development, with a pg_isready healthcheck the api and worker gate on and a named pgdata volume for persistence.

nodes.name: api
nodes.summary: Runs uvicorn against athena.api.app in the locally built image, overriding DATABASE_URL and FIXTURE_DATABASE_URL to point at the compose db service.

nodes.name: worker
nodes.summary: Runs the APScheduler ingestion worker (`python -m athena.worker.main`) from the same locally built image, sharing the compose database URLs.

nodes.name: dev-console
nodes.summary: Node 22 container that bind-mounts dev-console/ and runs the Vite dev server on 5173, proxying API calls to the api service.

nodes.name: deploy/docker-compose.yml
nodes.summary: Production stack that runs the prebuilt athena-backend:0.4.0 image as api and worker plus a cloudflared tunnel, all expose-only on the external urbanspace_intra network with a shared x-app-env anchor holding every runtime variable.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a YAML anchor (`x-app-env: &app_env`) so api and worker share one blank-valued environment block that the operator fills in once on the server.

nodes.name: api
nodes.summary: Production api container (athena-api) serving both the REST API and the bundled dashboard on port 8000, exposed only inside urbanspace_intra with restart: always.

nodes.name: worker
nodes.summary: Production worker container (athena-worker) running the daily external-API ingestion loop from the same image as api, differing only by command.

nodes.name: cloudflared
nodes.summary: Cloudflare Tunnel sidecar that publishes the internal stack outward using a TUNNEL_TOKEN, avoiding any host port mapping.

nodes.name: deploy/README.md
nodes.summary: Step-by-step production deployment runbook: ship the compose file and saved image tar to the server, create the external network, fill the x-app-env block, bring the stack up, and rebuild for a new version.

nodes.name: LIVE_API_VALIDATION.md

nodes.name: architecture.drawio

nodes.languageNotes: draw.io XML, not source code — a single 'Athena Architecture' diagram whose legend distinguishes external actors, adapters, AI agents, datastores, non-AI scheduled work and planned components.

nodes.name: alembic.ini

nodes.name: canva_oauth.py
nodes.summary: Operator script that mints a fresh Canva Connect access/refresh token pair through the OAuth 2.0 authorization-code + PKCE flow and persists it to the oauth_tokens row, recovering from a revoked single-use refresh-token lineage.
nodes.languageNotes: Canva refresh tokens are single-use and rotate, so concurrent refreshes revoke the whole lineage — this script is the only recovery path, and unlike the Google one it does write the new pair to the database.

nodes.name: build_authorize_url
nodes.summary: Assembles the Canva authorization URL with the requested scopes, the PKCE S256 challenge and a CSRF state parameter.

nodes.name: capture_code_via_server
nodes.summary: Runs a one-shot local HTTP server on the redirect URI to catch the authorization callback and return the captured query parameters.

nodes.name: exchange_code
nodes.summary: Posts the authorization code and PKCE verifier to Canva's token endpoint and returns the access/refresh token pair.

nodes.name: persist_to_db
nodes.summary: Writes the freshly minted Canva access and refresh tokens plus their expiry into the oauth_tokens row for provider "canva".

nodes.name: resolve_credentials
nodes.summary: Resolves the client id and secret from CLI flags, then environment variables, then the .env file loaded through athena.config.Settings.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: CLI entry point that parses arguments, drives the full consent-to-token flow, and either persists the result or prints it.

nodes.name: google_oauth.py
nodes.summary: Operator script that mints a Google refresh token for the reviews (business.manage) and/or ads (adwords) source through the desktop OAuth flow, verifies the granted scopes, and prints the .env line to paste — it never writes files.
nodes.languageNotes: Reviews and ads are separate grants because they usually belong to separate Google accounts; `--source both` requests both scopes in one consent when a single account owns them.

nodes.name: build_authorize_url
nodes.summary: Builds the Google authorization URL with the per-source scopes, PKCE challenge, state, and access_type=offline plus prompt=consent so a refresh token is always returned.

nodes.name: capture_code_via_server
nodes.summary: Serves the loopback redirect once to capture the authorization callback parameters from the browser.

nodes.name: _extract_code
nodes.summary: Validates the returned state against the expected CSRF value and pulls the authorization code out of the captured parameters.

nodes.name: exchange_code
nodes.summary: Exchanges the authorization code for tokens at Google's token endpoint and checks that the granted scopes match what was requested.

nodes.name: resolve_credentials
nodes.summary: Resolves the Google OAuth client id and secret from CLI flags, then environment variables, then .env via athena.config.Settings.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: CLI entry point that selects the source and its scopes, runs the consent flow, and prints the resulting refresh token as ready-to-paste .env lines.

nodes.name: meta_credentials.py
nodes.summary: Operator CLI that derives META_PAGE_ID, META_PAGE_TOKEN and META_IG_USER_ID from a Meta app id, app secret and short-lived user token by walking /debug_token, the long-lived token exchange, /me/accounts and instagram_business_account. It prints a ready-to-paste .env block only and never writes files, so it sits entirely outside the request path.
nodes.languageNotes: Imports GRAPH from athena.adapters.meta inside a try/except so the helper and the runtime adapter can never drift onto different Graph API versions, while still running before the package is importable.

nodes.name: zoho_oauth.py
nodes.summary: Operator CLI that exchanges a single-use Zoho self-client grant code for the non-rotating ZOHO_REFRESH_TOKEN used by the live Zoho adapter. It prints the token block for manual pasting into .env and never mutates files or participates in the request path.
nodes.languageNotes: Zoho's token endpoint reports failures as {"error": "<code>"} with HTTP 200, so the script translates codes through its own ERROR_HINTS table rather than trusting the status line.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Root package marker for the athena backend, carrying only the package version string (currently 0.4.0).

nodes.name: config.py
nodes.summary: Central pydantic-settings configuration for the whole backend: database URLs, the global and per-source live/fixture mode switches, credentials for Meta, Google Business Profile, Google Ads, Zoho, Google Places, Claude, Gemini and Canva, plus the resolution rules that decide which mode, which database and which OAuth grant serves each source.
nodes.languageNotes: env_ignore_empty=True is deliberate: bare keys in .env.example (VAR= with no value) must fall back to defaults instead of blanking string fields and crashing bool parsing.

nodes.name: logging_setup.py
nodes.summary: Installs a JSON-formatted stderr handler on the root logger and exposes the named-logger accessor every backend module uses for structured logging.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Empty package marker for the adapters layer, which fronts every external data source behind the shared live/fixture contract.

nodes.name: base.py
nodes.summary: Defines the contract every source adapter obeys: the SourceMode literal, the SourceAdapter abstract base whose fetch_live and fetch_fixture must return the same shape, and the shared error-envelope guard that turns an API's {"error": ...} body into a raised RuntimeError instead of a silent zero-row normalization.
nodes.languageNotes: The abstract base is what makes the live/fixture duality safe: normalize() has one code path because both backends are required to emit the documented live payload shape.

nodes.name: google_ads.py
nodes.summary: Google Ads Keyword Planner adapter that fetches keyword ideas either from customers.generateKeywordIdeas on the v24 Ads API or from the bundled fixture, then normalizes each keyword's latest monthly search volume into a weekly figure with a window date.
nodes.languageNotes: Monthly volumes are divided by a 4.345-week constant rather than a calendar month, so the weekly figure stays comparable across months of differing length.

nodes.name: google_auth.py
nodes.summary: Mints Google OAuth access tokens from the per-source refresh grant, validating up front that the grant carries the scope the caller's API actually needs (business.manage for reviews, adwords for ads) and turning every failure mode into an actionable message naming the script that re-mints the token.
nodes.languageNotes: The source argument is required rather than defaulted: reviews and ads resolve different refresh tokens, and a default would let a new call site silently authenticate against the wrong grant.

nodes.name: google_places.py
nodes.summary: Competitor Google reviews adapter reading Place Details from the Places API (New) with an automatic fallback to the legacy Place Details endpoint when the key's project is shut out of the new API, plus fixture-mode payloads keyed by competitor name.
nodes.languageNotes: The fallback is triggered only on the two configuration-shaped PERMISSION_DENIED reasons (SERVICE_DISABLED, API_KEY_SERVICE_BLOCKED); the legacy payload is reshaped into the (New) shape so normalize stays a single code path.

nodes.name: google_reviews.py
nodes.summary: Adapter for UrbanSpace's own Google Business Profile reviews, reading the legacy v4 My Business reviews endpoint in live mode or the bundled fixture otherwise, and normalizing the enum star ratings into integers.
nodes.languageNotes: Reviews exist only on the legacy v4 My Business API; live access additionally needs GBP API quota approval on the OAuth project.

nodes.name: meta.py
nodes.summary: The Meta adapter layer: three adapters covering UrbanSpace's own Facebook posts plus Instagram media and per-media insights, competitor Facebook Pages (gated behind Page Public Content Access), and competitor Instagram posts via Business Discovery. Each serves either the Graph API v25.0 or the bundled fixtures and normalizes both into the same post and comment row shapes.
nodes.languageNotes: Carousel posts expose no top-level media_url, so image resolution reads the first child item; Business Discovery exposes no comment text at all, which is why the IG competitor adapter has no comments stream.

nodes.name: parity.py
nodes.summary: Structural comparison harness that fingerprints a payload's shape and asserts a candidate does not deviate from a reference, used to prove that each adapter's fixture backend returns the same shape as its live API response.

nodes.name: zoho.py
nodes.summary: Zoho CRM chat-transcript adapter that refreshes its own OAuth token and reads the configured CRM module in live mode, or the bundled transcript fixture otherwise, normalizing each record into a transcript row with a creation-time window date.
nodes.languageNotes: Zoho reports failures as {"code", "message", "status": "error"} with no top-level "error" key, so the shared envelope guard never fires; the adapter checks status == "error" explicitly, and treats HTTP 204 as a genuinely empty result rather than a parse failure.

nodes.name: google_ads_keyword_ideas.json
nodes.summary: Fixture payload mirroring a Google Ads customers.generateKeywordIdeas response, with results carrying keyword text and monthlySearchVolumes so the keyword planner adapter can normalize offline.

nodes.name: google_competitor_reviews.json
nodes.summary: Fixture Google Places review payloads keyed by competitor name (Extra Space Asia, StorHub), each holding a place-level rating, rating count and review list in the Places API (New) shape.

nodes.name: google_reviews.json
nodes.summary: Fixture payload mirroring a Google Business Profile v4 reviews response for UrbanSpace's own location, including enum star ratings, reviewer names and the aggregate rating fields.

nodes.name: meta_competitor_comments.json
nodes.summary: Fixture Graph API comments payload for competitor Facebook posts, used by the competitor adapter's fixture comment stream since live comment text needs Page Public Content Access.

nodes.name: meta_competitor_posts.json
nodes.summary: Fixture Graph API /posts payload for competitor Facebook Pages, carrying message text, from-name, reaction and comment summaries in the shape the competitor adapter normalizes.

nodes.name: meta_ig_competitor.json
nodes.summary: Fixture Instagram Business Discovery payload wrapping a competitor's username and media list, matching the response the IG competitor adapter reads through UrbanSpace's own IG business account.

nodes.name: meta_ig_insights.json
nodes.summary: Fixture per-media Instagram insights keyed by media id, holding the reach, views, likes, comments and total_interactions metrics the own-posts adapter merges into each IG row.

nodes.name: meta_ig_media.json
nodes.summary: Fixture Graph API /media payload for UrbanSpace's own Instagram account, carrying captions, media type, permalinks and media URLs for the own-posts adapter.

nodes.name: meta_own_comments.json
nodes.summary: Fixture Graph API comments payload for UrbanSpace's own posts, feeding the own-posts adapter's separate comment stream that lands in PostComment rows.

nodes.name: meta_own_posts.json
nodes.summary: Fixture Graph API /posts payload for UrbanSpace's own Facebook Page, including message text, permalinks, attachments and reaction/comment/share summaries.

nodes.name: zoho_chats.json
nodes.summary: Fixture Zoho CRM module response holding chat transcript records with their creation times, used whenever the Zoho source runs in fixture mode.

nodes.name: Settings
nodes.summary: Pydantic BaseSettings model holding every backend setting and the logic that resolves them: source_mode_for collapses global and per-source mode overrides, database_url_for and active_database_url route each source to the live or fixture database, ingestion_skipped_for names the one degenerate single-DB config, and google_refresh_token_for picks the right OAuth grant.
nodes.languageNotes: Global fixture mode overrides every per-source setting on purpose: per-source overrides take effect only in live mode, which is what stops a live-pinned source leaking rows into the fixture database.

nodes.name: configure_logging
nodes.summary: Replaces the root logger's handlers with a single stderr handler using a JSON formatter that renames levelname to level, then applies the requested log level.

nodes.name: get_logger
nodes.summary: Returns a named logger, the accessor every backend module uses so log records carry a module-scoped name.

nodes.name: raise_on_error_envelope
nodes.summary: Raises a RuntimeError when an API response body is an {"error": ...} envelope and otherwise returns it unchanged, so a failed call surfaces immediately instead of normalizing to zero rows.

nodes.name: SourceAdapter
nodes.summary: Abstract base for every external source: subclasses declare a source name and implement fetch_live, fetch_fixture and normalize, while fetch dispatches on the adapter's mode and fetch_normalized composes the two. Both backends are contractually required to return the same payload shape.

nodes.name: KeywordPlannerAdapter
nodes.summary: Source adapter for Google Ads keyword volumes: posts the configured tracked keywords to customers.generateKeywordIdeas in live mode, loads the keyword-ideas fixture otherwise, and normalizes the latest monthly search volume of each result into a weekly figure.

nodes.name: google_access_token
nodes.summary: Exchanges the refresh token belonging to a named Google source for an access token, rejecting a missing grant, an unreachable or non-JSON token endpoint, an OAuth error body, and a grant whose echoed scopes do not cover the source's required scope.
nodes.languageNotes: Checking the scopes Google echoes on the refresh grant catches the commonest misconfiguration — one API's token pasted into the other's variable — before the first real API call.

nodes.name: _new_api_unavailable
nodes.summary: Returns true only when a Places API (New) error body carries a SERVICE_DISABLED or API_KEY_SERVICE_BLOCKED reason, the two configuration-shaped denials that justify falling back to the legacy endpoint rather than raising.

nodes.name: GooglePlacesReviewsAdapter
nodes.summary: Source adapter for competitor Google reviews: reads Place Details from the Places API (New) with a legacy-endpoint fallback reshaped into the same payload, serves the competitor-keyed fixture otherwise, and normalizes place rating, rating count and up to five reviews into rows with deterministic hash ids.

nodes.name: GoogleReviewsAdapter
nodes.summary: Source adapter for UrbanSpace's own Google Business Profile reviews, reading the v4 accounts/locations/reviews endpoint with an OAuth access token in live mode or the reviews fixture otherwise, and mapping enum star ratings to integers.

nodes.name: MetaOwnPostsAdapter
nodes.summary: Source adapter for UrbanSpace's own Meta presence: fetches Facebook Page posts, Instagram media and per-media insights (or their fixtures), normalizes both platforms into one post row shape with likes, views and interaction counts, and exposes a separate comment stream.
nodes.languageNotes: Meta's media URLs are signed and expire in roughly a day, so images are downloaded once at ingestion time rather than referenced by URL.

nodes.name: MetaCompetitorAdapter
nodes.summary: Source adapter for competitor Facebook Page posts and comments, normalizing message text with reaction and comment counts. Its live path refuses to run unless competitor_live_access_enabled is set, because it needs Page Public Content Access.

nodes.name: MetaIGCompetitorAdapter
nodes.summary: Source adapter for competitor Instagram posts via Business Discovery, queried through UrbanSpace's own IG business account so it needs no Page Public Content Access. Business Discovery exposes no comment text, so it carries posts only.

nodes.name: shape_of
nodes.summary: Recursively reduces a payload to a structural fingerprint: dicts become key-to-shape maps, lists become the shape of their first element, and leaves become their type name.

nodes.name: assert_same_shape
nodes.summary: Public entry point of the parity harness: fingerprints a reference and a candidate payload and raises AssertionError when the candidate deviates structurally.

nodes.name: _compare
nodes.summary: Walks two shape fingerprints in parallel, asserting matching container kinds and the presence of every reference key, and reporting the JSON-style path of the first deviation.

nodes.name: ZohoChatsAdapter
nodes.summary: Source adapter for Zoho CRM chat transcripts: refreshes an OAuth access token against the configured data centre, reads the configured module and transcript field, and normalizes each record into a transcript row. Fixture mode serves the bundled chats payload instead.

nodes.name: _format_error
nodes.summary: Renders a Graph API error object into an operator-facing message, appending the actionable hint keyed by the Meta error code and the trace id when present.

nodes.name: graph_get
nodes.summary: Performs a Graph API GET against the version pinned by the runtime adapter, exiting with a formatted message on a transport failure, a non-JSON body, or an error envelope.

nodes.name: check_token
nodes.summary: Validates a /debug_token response: rejects an invalid token, a token minted for a different app id, and an APP-type token that cannot read Page posts or IG insights.

nodes.name: report_scopes
nodes.summary: Prints which of the five required Meta scopes the token carries, naming the adapter call each missing scope would break and listing any extra scopes granted.

nodes.name: exchange_for_long_lived
nodes.summary: Exchanges a short-lived user token for a long-lived (~60 day) one via grant_type=fb_exchange_token, the only step needing the app id and secret and a prerequisite for minting a never-expiring Page token.

nodes.name: list_pages
nodes.summary: Pages through /me/accounts to collect every Facebook Page the account administers together with its own Page access token.

nodes.name: choose_page
nodes.summary: Selects the Page to derive credentials from, honouring an explicit --page-id, auto-selecting when only one Page is administered, and otherwise listing the candidates and exiting so the operator can pick.

nodes.name: verify_with_adapter
nodes.summary: Optional --verify step that constructs the real MetaOwnPostsAdapter in live mode with the derived credentials and reports the normalized row count, so the printed values are proven before the operator trusts them.

nodes.name: resolve_credentials
nodes.summary: Resolves the app id, app secret and user access token from CLI flags falling back to the META_APP_* environment variables, exiting with the names of whatever is still missing.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: CLI driver that parses arguments, inspects and reports on the supplied token, exchanges it for a long-lived one, picks the Page, resolves the linked IG business account, re-confirms the Page token has no expiry, and prints the .env block plus an optional adapter verification.

nodes.name: resolve_credentials
nodes.summary: Resolves the Zoho self-client id, secret and data centre from CLI flags falling back to Settings (and therefore .env), exiting with the missing variable names.

nodes.name: exchange_code
nodes.summary: Posts the grant code to the data-centre-specific Zoho token endpoint and returns the token body, translating Zoho's bare {"error": code} responses — which often arrive with HTTP 200 — into actionable messages.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: CLI driver that resolves credentials, prompts for (or accepts) the single-use grant code, performs the exchange, and prints the ZOHO_REFRESH_TOKEN block for manual pasting into .env.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Empty package marker for athena.ai, the LangGraph and Claude agent layer that turns ingested marketing data into research findings and generated content.

nodes.name: agents.py
nodes.summary: Runtime prompt resolution for the AI agents: reads an agent definition from the database and composes its effective system prompt from the stored prompt plus its ordered skill fragments.

nodes.name: images.py
nodes.summary: Image-generation seam for the pipeline: a Protocol, a live Gemini-backed client, and a deterministic placeholder client, chosen by whether an image API key is configured.

nodes.name: llm.py
nodes.summary: LLM seam for structured output: Claude Sonnet through langchain-anthropic in live mode, or a FakeLLM preloaded with one canned instance per schema when no API key is set (the dashboard's "Sample AI").

nodes.summary: Central TypeScript contract for every backend payload the dashboard consumes: KPI snapshots and engagement summaries, the four research responses (trends, customer chats, social, competitors), post generation input/output, settings rows (competitors, keywords, agents, skills), raw ingest tables, and the /config/modes shape that drives the Live vs Fixture badges.

nodes.name: vite-env.d.ts
nodes.summary: Single triple-slash reference pulling in Vite's client ambient types so asset imports and import.meta.env type-check.

nodes.name: TagPill.tsx

nodes.name: useApi.ts
nodes.summary: The dashboard's two data-fetching hooks. useApi fetches on mount and exposes reload for retries; useCachedApi layers the 24-hour localStorage cache over it so repeat visits to AI-backed endpoints spend no AI credits until the user presses a refresh button.
nodes.languageNotes: Both hooks keep the latest `fn` in a ref so an inline arrow callback does not retrigger the effect, and use an `alive` flag in the cleanup to avoid setState after unmount.

nodes.name: agentDefaults.ts
nodes.summary: Built-in fallback system prompts and skill-key sets for the eight Athena agents (caption writer, image prompt designer, title suggester, customer/social/competitor/comment analysts, aggregator), shown in the Settings view when the backend has no stored override.

nodes.name: AiCard
nodes.summary: Card shell for AI content: sparkle icon, title, the AI status badge, an optional red tag pill and an action slot, followed by the caller's children.

nodes.name: AsyncSection
nodes.summary: Renders a progress bar while the query loads, an error note with a Retry button on failure, and otherwise calls the render-prop children with the resolved data.

nodes.name: ConfidenceBadge
nodes.summary: Colour-codes a 1-5 confidence score and attaches an info dot whose tooltip shows the model's reason for that score.

nodes.name: Ico
nodes.summary: Renders the named SVG string from the ICO registry inline via dangerouslySetInnerHTML.

nodes.summary: Computes the clamped percentage from step over total and renders either a determinate fill with the step label or an animated indeterminate bar with a generic label.

nodes.name: TagPill

nodes.name: useApi
nodes.summary: Fetch-on-mount hook returning data, error, loading and reload. Keeps the fetcher in a ref so inline callbacks do not retrigger it, guards against setState after unmount, and re-runs when deps or the reload tick change.

nodes.name: useCachedApi
nodes.summary: useApi plus the 24-hour localStorage cache: a fresh entry renders instantly with no network call at all, and reload deletes the entry before refetching. Intended for AI-backed GETs only, so repeat visits do not re-spend AI credits.

nodes.name: api.test.ts
nodes.summary: Vitest suite for the dashboard API client, pinning the count-then-tail pagination behaviour of /data lists, ApiError status and FastAPI detail propagation, 204 handling and competitor query-param encoding.

nodes.name: api.ts
nodes.summary: Typed fetch client for the whole Athena backend — weekly KPI, research topics, /data row lists, post generation and drafts, Canva handoff, ingestion triggers and /config CRUD — plus NDJSON streaming variants for the long-running AI calls.
nodes.languageNotes: A generic request<T> wrapper plus listTail, which reads the row count with a limit=1 probe and then fetches the last DATA_LIMIT rows, because /data lists are id-ascending with no 'latest' parameter.

nodes.name: cache.test.ts
nodes.summary: Vitest suite for the localStorage AI cache, covering set/get roundtrip, expiry and corrupt-entry eviction, prefix deletion, and the fail-open behaviour when storage throws.

nodes.name: cache.ts
nodes.summary: Fail-open localStorage store behind the dashboard's 24-hour client-side AI response cache: versioned, TTL-stamped entries under an 'athena:cache:v1:' prefix so repeat visits render instantly without re-spending AI credits.
nodes.languageNotes: Every entry point is wrapped in try/catch so private-browsing or quota errors degrade to a cache miss rather than breaking the view.

nodes.name: cacheKeys.ts
nodes.summary: Single source of truth for the AI cache keys consumed by useCachedApi, shared so a view's cache key and the Research refresh cache-bust can never drift apart.

nodes.name: derive.test.ts
nodes.summary: Vitest suite for the client-side analytics helpers, especially the week-over-week window matching rules — adjacent daily snapshots must not count as 'last week' — and keyword first-appearance versus percentage change.

nodes.name: derive.ts
nodes.summary: Client-side analytics over raw /data rows: newest-first ordering, week-over-week KPI deltas for the Home tiles, per-keyword search-volume change, and per-platform competitor activity stats.
nodes.languageNotes: Week-over-week comparison picks the window closest to 7 days back within a 5-9 day tolerance, so daily snapshots never masquerade as a previous week.

nodes.name: exportPng.test.ts
nodes.summary: Vitest suite for PNG export, stubbing canvas 2d context and Image to assert cover-crop geometry, the branded-background fallback when the AI image fails to load, and the error callbacks for unsupported canvas and null toBlob.

nodes.name: exportPng.ts
nodes.summary: Renders a generated post to a 1080x1080 PNG on an offscreen canvas and triggers a browser download, cover-cropping the AI image or falling back to the platform brand colour with a decorative circle.

nodes.name: fmt.ts
nodes.summary: Compact number formatter for KPI tiles and metric badges, turning 2500000 into '2.5M' and 11800 into '11.8k'.

nodes.name: splitHashtags.ts
nodes.summary: Separates a generated caption's body text from hashtags found anywhere in it so the two render on their own lines instead of running together inline.

nodes.name: stream.test.ts
nodes.summary: Vitest suite for the NDJSON stream reader, covering progress-then-result resolution, error-event and non-ok rejection, streams that end without a result, and line reassembly across chunk boundaries.

nodes.name: stream.ts
nodes.summary: Consumes the backend's NDJSON streaming endpoints, forwarding progress events to a callback so long AI jobs can render a real step-labelled progress bar, and resolving with the terminal result event's payload.
nodes.languageNotes: Buffers partial lines across reader chunks and cancels the reader on failure so an aborted stream never leaks a locked body.

nodes.name: GenerateProvider.tsx

nodes.languageNotes: Exports the shared PLATFORMS/TONES/LENGTHS/AUDIENCES/STYLES option lists and PLACEHOLDER_PNG_B64, which is kept in sync with backend/src/athena/ai/images.py purely to detect drafts still showing the image-failure placeholder.

nodes.name: ModesProvider.tsx
nodes.summary: React context provider that fetches GET /config/modes once per app load, supplying the live-versus-fixture state that drives the green 'Live' / amber 'Fixture' dot on data sections and 'Live AI' versus 'Sample AI' on AI sections.
nodes.languageNotes: Held in memory only, never cached, so an env change is reflected on reload; a failed fetch leaves modes undefined and StatusBadge simply renders nothing.

nodes.name: ToastProvider.tsx
nodes.summary: React context provider exposing a toast(msg) function and rendering the app-wide aria-live toast element that auto-dismisses after two seconds.

nodes.name: useGenerate.ts
nodes.summary: Consumer hook for GenerateContext that throws when used outside GenerateProvider, giving views a non-optional context value.

nodes.name: useModes.ts
nodes.summary: Consumer hook reading the live-versus-fixture modes from ModesContext for status badges across the dashboard.

nodes.name: useToast.ts
nodes.summary: Consumer hook returning the toast function from ToastContext so any component can raise a transient notification.

nodes.name: theme.css
nodes.summary: The dashboard's single global stylesheet: CSS custom-property brand palette, reset, sidebar shell, cards, buttons, chips, KPI tiles, hero draft actions and the toast, all keyed off hand-written class names used directly in the view components.
nodes.languageNotes: Colour roles are declared once as :root custom properties (--ora, --blue, --ai and their light/dark variants) so views reference semantic tokens rather than hex values.

nodes.name: ChipRow.tsx
nodes.summary: Generic single-select chip row used throughout the Generate brief form for platform, tone, length and audience choices.

nodes.name: ToggleChip.tsx
nodes.summary: Two-state chip button for the Generate brief's boolean content flags (hashtags, call to action, emoji, pricing).

nodes.name: ApiError
nodes.summary: Error subclass carrying the HTTP status alongside the message, so callers can branch on status and surface FastAPI's detail field.

nodes.name: request
nodes.summary: Generic JSON fetch wrapper that applies the API base URL and content-type header, raises ApiError with FastAPI's detail on non-ok responses, and resolves undefined for 204.

nodes.name: cacheGet
nodes.summary: Reads a cached AI response, evicting and reporting a miss for corrupt, wrong-version or expired entries and for any storage error.

nodes.name: cacheSet
nodes.summary: Stores a value with a version marker and absolute expiry, defaulting to the 24-hour TTL, silently no-oping when storage is unavailable or full.

nodes.name: cacheDelete
nodes.summary: Removes a single cached entry, used by the refresh buttons to force a fresh AI call.

nodes.name: cacheDeletePrefix
nodes.summary: Evicts every cached entry under a key prefix, used to clear a whole family of AI responses such as all per-competitor results.

nodes.name: newestFirst
nodes.summary: Returns a copy of any windowed row list sorted by window_date descending, so 'recent' views can rely on server-side id ordering being irrelevant.

nodes.name: kpiDeltas
nodes.summary: Computes week-over-week percentage deltas for views, likes, interactions and post count by comparing the newest window against the window closest to seven days earlier.
nodes.languageNotes: Returns null rather than a misleading number when no window sits 5-9 days back, which is what keeps the Home 'vs last week' badges from comparing adjacent daily snapshots.

nodes.name: keywordChanges
nodes.summary: Builds a per-keyword week-over-week change map from the two most recent search-volume windows, tagging first appearances as new and omitting keywords that stayed at zero.

nodes.name: competitorPlatformStats
nodes.summary: Aggregates one competitor's posts for a single platform into posts tracked, last active date, total comments and the three highest-engagement recent posts.

nodes.name: downloadPostPNG
nodes.summary: Draws a 1080x1080 post image onto an offscreen canvas — cover-cropping the AI image or painting the platform brand colour with a decorative circle — then triggers a timestamped PNG download.
nodes.languageNotes: Every failure path routes through the optional onError callback (wired to the toast) rather than throwing, so a bad image degrades to a branded export instead of a broken button.

nodes.name: fmt
nodes.summary: Formats a count as a compact metric string with M or k suffixes, trimming a trailing .0 and falling back to locale grouping below a thousand.

nodes.name: splitHashtags
nodes.summary: Splits caption text into a body string and a hashtag list, collecting tags from anywhere in the text rather than only from a trailing block.

nodes.name: streamNdjson

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Athena ingests UrbanSpace's marketing data (Meta posts and comments, Google Business reviews, Google Ads keyword volumes, Zoho CRM chat transcripts), runs AI research and content generation over it, and serves the results as a marketing dashboard. Read the README first for the two audiences it addresses: the marketing team's four dashboard views, and the developer's map of a three-app monorepo (backend/ for the API and worker, frontend/ for the dashboard, dev-console/ for internal debugging). The architecture diagram draws the same pipeline end to end, and the rest of this tour walks that pipeline in the order the data actually travels: external APIs, adapters, ingestion, Postgres, features, AI, HTTP, dashboard.

tour.title: Configuration and Source Modes
tour.description: Before any code makes sense, you need the project's central design decision: every data source can run in either live mode (real API calls) or fixture mode (bundled sample data shaped identically). config.py is the pydantic-settings object that holds database URLs, the global and per-source mode switches, and credentials for Meta, Google Business Profile, Google Ads, Zoho, Google Places, Claude, Gemini and Canva, plus the rules that resolve which mode, which database and which OAuth grant serves each source. Miss this and nothing downstream will explain why almost every source has a fixture twin. The .env.example file is the practical companion listing what a developer actually has to fill in.
tour.languageLesson: pydantic-settings reads a typed Settings class from environment variables and .env files, validating and coercing each field on construction. Because the class is ordinary Python, computed properties can express derived policy — here, resolving a per-source mode from a global default plus source-specific overrides — so the resolution rules live with the settings rather than being re-derived at each call site.

tour.title: Source Adapters and Their Fixtures
tour.description: Adapters are where the live-versus-fixture switch from Step 2 becomes concrete. base.py defines the contract every source obeys: a SourceMode literal, a SourceAdapter abstract base whose fetch_live and fetch_fixture must return the same row shape, and a shared error-envelope guard that raises on an API's error body instead of quietly normalizing zero rows. The Meta adapter is the most involved — own Facebook posts, Instagram media and insights, competitor Pages behind Page Public Content Access, competitor Instagram via Business Discovery — while the Google Ads and Zoho adapters follow the same two-path pattern against Keyword Planner and CRM transcripts. Alongside them sit the JSON fixtures that the fixture path reads, which is why demo mode looks exactly like production.
tour.languageLesson: Python's abc module turns a base class into a contract: methods marked @abstractmethod cannot be left unimplemented by a subclass without the class failing to instantiate. Pairing that with a Literal type for the mode gives you a closed set of valid values a type checker can exhaustively verify, so a new source cannot silently forget its fixture path.

tour.title: Two Databases, One Dashboard
tour.description: This is the most surprising thing in the backend, and it follows directly from Step 2. Rather than forcing the whole system into live or fixture mode, db/base.py keeps two Postgres databases and defines RoutedSession, which binds each source-owned table to whichever database that source's effective mode selects. A single dashboard page can therefore show live Meta data next to fixture Zoho data, each labelled honestly. bootstrap.py handles the consequence at startup: it creates the target database when missing, migrates it to Alembic head, seeds defaults, then repeats the whole sequence for the fixture database when a second one is configured.
tour.languageLesson: SQLAlchemy sessions normally bind to one engine, but a Session accepts a `binds` mapping from mapped class to engine, resolved per query. That is the seam RoutedSession exploits — the ORM models stay unaware of routing, and the decision about which physical database answers a query is made once, at session construction.

tour.title: The Data Model and Migrations
tour.description: models.py declares the SQLAlchemy ORM classes for every table the routing layer in Step 4 dispatches over: ingested source rows, generated content, and the runtime-editable config tables. The Alembic migration history is the authoritative schema — 0001_core.py creates the original ingestion tables, where own_posts and competitor_posts are both keyed by (source_id, window_date) so re-ingesting a window updates rather than duplicates. The later config-tables migration adds competitors, tracked keywords, agent definitions and skills, which is what makes the dashboard's Settings view able to change pipeline behaviour without a deploy.
tour.languageLesson: Alembic migrations form an ordered chain, each naming its predecessor via down_revision, so the schema's history is a linked list rather than a folder of loose files. A natural key such as (source_id, window_date) with a unique constraint is what makes an ingestion upsert idempotent: rerunning yesterday's job corrects rows instead of duplicating them.

tour.title: Scheduled Ingestion
tour.description: The worker is the second of the three application entry points and the thing that actually moves data from the adapters in Step 3 into the tables in Step 5. worker/main.py configures logging, optionally bootstraps the database, registers jobs and starts the APScheduler loop; scheduler.py is a small registry that collects named cron-scheduled callables through a decorator and also offers a run-now path for on-demand triggers. ingestion_jobs.py declares the six jobs (Meta own posts, competitor posts, Google reviews, competitor reviews, keyword volumes, Zoho chats) with their cron expressions, and each one delegates to runner.py, a generic driver that pulls normalized rows from any adapter and upserts them, reporting inserted-versus-updated counts.
tour.languageLesson: A decorator-based registry is a common Python pattern for plugin-style wiring: the decorator records the function in a module-level collection at import time, so adding a job means writing one decorated function rather than editing a central list. The cost is that the module must actually be imported for its jobs to exist, which is why the worker imports the jobs package explicitly.

tour.title: The AI Seams
tour.description: The same live-versus-sample duality that governs data sources also governs AI, and this is what the dashboard means by 'Live AI' versus 'Sample AI'. llm.py exposes one structured-output seam: Claude Sonnet through langchain-anthropic when an API key is present, or a FakeLLM preloaded with one canned instance per schema when it is not. images.py mirrors that shape for image generation with a live Gemini client and a deterministic placeholder. schemas.py holds the Pydantic result models the LLM is asked to fill in, and agents.py composes each agent's effective system prompt at runtime from its stored database definition plus its ordered skill fragments — which is how Settings edits reach the model without a redeploy.
tour.languageLesson: typing.Protocol gives structural typing: a class satisfies the Protocol by having the right methods, with no inheritance and no registration. That is what lets the live client and the fake sit behind one seam that a type checker still verifies, and it keeps the fake free of any dependency on the SDK the live client needs.

tour.title: Feature Layer and the Canva Handoff
tour.description: Features are where the stored rows from Step 5 meet the AI clients from Step 7. research.py backs all four research tabs — keyword trends, customer questions mined from Zoho transcripts, own social and Google review insights, per-competitor analysis — each finishing with LLM-suggested post titles. aggregate.py is a LangGraph supervisor that fans out to those four analysts concurrently and synthesises their findings into recommendations, streaming per-node progress events as it goes; generate.py builds a three-node graph per post option (caption, then image prompt, then image). The generated image is then handed to Canva, whose client uploads the asset, creates a design to obtain an edit URL, and later pulls the edited result back — the handoff that drafts.py persists.
tour.languageLesson: LangGraph models an AI workflow as a directed graph of nodes over a shared state object rather than a chain of calls. Independent nodes can run concurrently, and because each node transition is an observable event, the same graph that computes the answer can also emit the step-labelled progress the dashboard renders.

tour.title: The FastAPI Surface
tour.description: app.py is the first of the three entry points and the target uvicorn runs: an application factory that configures logging, bootstraps the database in a lifespan hook (the Step 4 sequence), exposes /health, mounts six routers, and serves the built dashboard as static files at the root — which is why one container answers both the API and the UI. deps.py supplies request-scoped dependencies: settings, the routed session factory from Step 4, and the LLM, image and Canva clients from Steps 7 and 8, each imported lazily so a missing optional dependency only breaks the routes that need it. schemas.py holds the Pydantic request and response models for the whole surface. Of the routers, /research exposes the five research features and /config carries both the settings CRUD and the modes report the dashboard depends on.
tour.languageLesson: FastAPI's Depends system builds a dependency graph per request and caches each provider's result within that request, so asking for the same session in three places yields one session. A lifespan async context manager gives startup and shutdown a single scope, which is the right home for work like database bootstrapping that must finish before the first request is served.

tour.title: Dashboard Shell and State
tour.description: The third entry point starts the marketing dashboard: main.tsx mounts App under StrictMode with the global theme stylesheet, and App.tsx nests the Toast, Modes and Generate providers around a collapsible sidebar switching between Home, Research, Generate and Settings. types.ts is the frontend's half of the contract with Step 9's Pydantic schemas — every backend payload the dashboard consumes, hand-written and therefore worth checking when an API response changes. GenerateProvider owns the entire Generate workflow as context: the brief form state, the streamed generation with progress, the cached recommendations and every draft action, which is why GenerateView can stay a rendering surface over shared state rather than holding it itself.
tour.languageLesson: React context plus a custom hook is the idiomatic way to share workflow state without prop drilling: the provider owns the state and the hook is the only sanctioned way to read it, so a component that consumes it outside the provider fails loudly. Splitting the hook into its own module (useGenerate.ts) also keeps the provider file fast-refresh friendly.

tour.title: Crossing the HTTP Seam
tour.description: This is the step that ties the two halves of the repo together, because the seam between them is HTTP rather than imports. lib/api.ts is a single typed fetch client covering the whole backend and carrying roughly forty calls into the endpoints from Step 9, with NDJSON streaming variants for the long AI jobs. Trace one feature all the way through: ResearchView mounts the Trends tab, TrendsTab asks useApi for the data, api.ts issues GET /research/internet-trends, the router calls the research feature from Step 8, which reads keyword rows ingested by the Step 6 worker from the Google Ads adapter in Step 3. Every other research tab is the same path with a different adapter at the far end.
tour.languageLesson: TypeScript generics let one fetch wrapper stay type-safe across every route: the function is parameterised by its response type, so callers get a checked shape without a cast per call. Note that this type safety is asserted, not proven — the compiler trusts the annotation, so the frontend types and the backend's Pydantic schemas have to be kept in step by hand or by test.

tour.title: Provenance Badges and Section States
tour.description: Here the mode switch from Step 2 finally surfaces to the user. ModesProvider fetches GET /config/modes once per app load, and StatusBadge turns that snapshot into the dot every section carries: green Live for real service data, amber Fixture for bundled samples, Live AI or Sample AI for AI blocks. AsyncSection wraps each section in its own loading, error-with-retry and success states so one failing panel never blanks a whole view, and upgrades its bar to a real step-labelled progress indicator when handed streaming progress. cache.ts is the fail-open localStorage store behind the 24-hour AI response cache, which is why revisiting Research is instant and does not re-spend AI credits until the user presses refresh.
tour.languageLesson: Rendering per-section state instead of one page-level spinner is a deliberate composition choice: each section is its own async boundary, so partial failure degrades one panel rather than the screen. Making the cache fail-open matters for the same reason — a browser with localStorage disabled or full should lose caching, not the feature.

tour.title: The Internal Dev Console
tour.description: The repo holds two React apps, and conflating them is the easiest mistake to make. dev-console/ is an internal debugging UI, not a second copy of the dashboard: it has its own bootstrap, a five-tab shell, and its own typed client hitting the same backend from Step 9, with a base URL from VITE_API_BASE so it can point at a local or deployed API. Its distinguishing feature is the Data & Ingest tab, which shows raw table rows and fires the POST /ingest/{source} triggers by hand rather than waiting for the Step 6 cron. Both frontend apps carry Vitest suites — the dev console's App test is a good entry point for how components here are tested against a mocked client.
tour.languageLesson: Vite exposes only environment variables prefixed with VITE_ to client code, and they are inlined at build time rather than read at runtime — so pointing a built console at a different backend means rebuilding, not restarting. That build-time substitution is also why a secret must never be given a VITE_ prefix.

tour.title: Packaging and Deployment
tour.description: The Dockerfile builds one image for the whole system: a node:22-alpine stage runs the frontend build, then a python:3.12-slim stage installs the backend with uv and copies in the compiled dashboard, which is what app.py serves statically in Step 9. The development compose file builds that image from source and runs Postgres, the API, the worker and a hot-reloading dev console together, while the deploy compose file runs a pinned prebuilt image as api and worker behind a Cloudflare tunnel with no host port mapping. Read the deploy runbook for the sequence an operator actually follows, and the live-API validation checklist for the state of each external integration — the record of which sources can genuinely run live is what makes the fixture path from Step 3 a permanent design feature rather than temporary scaffolding.
tour.languageLesson: A multi-stage Docker build lets one file hold several FROM stages and copy only the artifacts forward, so Node and the frontend toolchain never reach the runtime image. Layer order matters for caching: dependency installation should sit above the source copy, or every code edit invalidates the dependency layer and reinstalls everything.
